recipe.visualDefinition: A high-contrast 1960s-style album cover featuring a split lower section with a square portrait on the left and a tracklist on the right, topped by a dominant black header containing centered typography.
coreVisualRelationships: Vertical hierarchy from large title to smaller subtitle
Horizontal split between photographic subject and textual list
Color-coded text alternating between gold and light blue
Thin white framing lines separating the lower quadrants
coreInvariants: Solid black background for the top half
Square-cropped portrait with neutral studio background
Strictly centered alignment for the top text block

compositionAndHierarchy.subjectPositionAndScale: Portrait occupies the bottom-left quadrant, approximately 45% of the total width.
compositionAndHierarchy.visualAnchor: The artist's name in large, light blue serif capitals.
compositionAndHierarchy.movementAndEyePath: Starts at the top center title, moves down to the artist name, then scans the portrait before reading the tracklist on the right.
compositionAndHierarchy.negativeSpace: Heavy use of solid black in the upper half creates a dramatic, stage-like focus.

colorSystem.dominantColorRole: Solid black background for depth and contrast.
colorSystem.contrastColorRole: Light blue (Cyan) for the primary artist name and alternating list items.
colorSystem.accentColorRole: Warm gold/yellow for the title and secondary list items.
colorSystem.saturationAndValueRelationship: High value contrast between the bright text and the dark background; muted, naturalistic tones in the photograph.
paletteRestrictions: Limit to black, white, cyan, and gold

typographyAndGraphicLanguage.baseSkeleton: Geometric sans-serif and high-contrast transitional serif.
letterConstructionRules: All-caps for primary and secondary titles
Title case for the third-level subtitle
Uniform stroke weight for sans-serif elements
characterSpecificRedesigns: Thin horizontal line underlining the main title
Tight tracking on the tracklist items
typographyAndGraphicLanguage.pairingStrategy: Serif for the name to convey elegance; Sans-serif for titles and lists to provide modern clarity.

candidateDirections.reason: Matches the high-contrast serif look of the artist name.
Matches the utilitarian sans-serif used for the tracklist.

twoStageComposition.backgroundInstruction: Generate a split-screen layout with a solid black top half and a bottom half divided into two sections by thin white lines. The bottom-left section should contain a square studio portrait of a person with a 1960s hairstyle against a light grey background. The bottom-right section should be solid black.
twoStageComposition.overlayInstruction: Add centered text in the top black area using a gold sans-serif for the top line and a large light blue serif for the second line. Add a vertical list of text in the bottom-right section, alternating colors between gold and light blue for each line.

verificationChecks: Is the artist name the largest text element?
Does the tracklist alternate colors line-by-line?
Is there a thin white border separating the portrait from the list?

adjustableVariables: Number of tracks in the list
postGenerationChecks: Ensure the top text is perfectly centered.
Check that the white framing lines are thin and crisp.
Verify the serif font has high stroke contrast.
Confirm the portrait is a perfect square or near-square.
recipe.reuseFormula: Black Header + Large Serif Name + Split Bottom (Square Photo | Vertical List)
